feedback:
Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. The candidate keeps the iteration 7 design (score 219.96, the best raced so far) and changes one field: controller.base_speed from 1.6 to 1.8. Geometry (outer sensors at x = ±0.04, y = 0.05; inner three at y = 0.03; sensor_size 0.012) and all gains (kp 3.0, ki 0.05, kd 0.5, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], line_loss last_direction) are unchanged. It is valid against the contract.

The evidence behind the step: raising base_speed from 1.4 to 1.6 (iteration 7) lifted the score from 173.5 to 219.96. Oval completions rose from 2 of 20 to 6 of 20, oval progress rose from 0.74 to 0.76, and s-bend progress rose from 0.32 to 0.36. Line loss stayed at about 1.0 per run on every track, as in every raced iteration, so speed did not worsen it. The condition in the earlier rule (completions rising with score above 173.5 and progress held) is met, so one further step is justified.

Risks to read in the race. A faster robot reaches the 0.06 m off-track limit sooner on bends. The s-bend and slalom are the tracks most exposed: s-bend progress is the one most likely to fall, and slalom progress (about 0.08) is already very low and is not expected to be limited by speed. Line loss is still the unresolved fault, and it has not responded to kp, kd, footprint or spread.

What to do after the race, depending on the result:
- If oval progress falls below about 0.70 or s-bend progress falls below about 0.30, speed is now causing early exits. Revert base_speed to 1.6 and test controller.ki at 0.15 next.
- If oval completions reach 8 or more and the score exceeds 220 with s-bend progress held, keep 1.8 and consider a small further step (1.9) in a later iteration only.
- If completions do not rise but progress holds, speed is not the binding limit at this point; keep 1.8 and move to the line-loss lever (ki) rather than speed.
